i.norm: Verifies that flattening a sparse argument array containing "-Z&=" (where "Z" is a known option requiring an argument) splits the token into ["-Z", "&="], and that applying flatten a second time on that already-split result produces the same two elements. The input array has six slots; only index 4 is set to "-Z&=". During the first flatten call PosixParser bursts "-Z&=" into the option token "-Z" and its argument value "&=", discarding the five null slots. The second flatten call receives the clean ["-Z", "&="] pair and leaves it unchanged, confirming idempotent behaviour once the tokens are already separated.
Register option "Z" as one that accepts an argument value.
Build a sparse six-element argument array; only the fifth slot contains a token. "-Z&=" encodes option Z with the attached argument value "&=".
First flatten: null slots are ignored; "-Z&=" is burst into "-Z" and "&=".
Second flatten: the already-separated tokens pass through unchanged.
